skill.name: claude-reflect
skill.description: Captures Claude Code corrections, queues possible learnings, and helps users review them before updating CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md memory files.
skill.summary: Review and apply Claude Code learnings from corrections, session history, and repeated tool errors.
skill.author: BayramAnnakov

security_audit.summary: This skill intentionally reads and writes Claude Code memory files, queues user corrections, and can scan local session history under the user home directory. Most confirmed findings are privacy, local persistence, and external CLI analysis risks tied to the core feature, while documentation, tests, /dev/null redirects, and the reviewed JPEG asset are false positives. No evidence found of network exfiltration code or prompt-injection text that tries to bypass this audit.

remediation.issue: Automatic capture can persist sensitive user prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Require clear install-time consent, redact secrets before queueing, and avoid storing full prompt text when a shorter learning is enough.

remediation.issue: History scanning reads Claude Code session files.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact session files before scanning, default to the current project, and require confirmation for broad or all-project scans.

remediation.issue: Tool error extraction can capture environment and credential context.
remediation.suggestion: Redact values for API_KEY, SECRET, DATABASE_URL, *_URL, and service tokens before display, storage, or semantic validation.

remediation.issue: Semantic validation sends captured text to the Claude CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Document the data flow, add an opt-out flag, and skip semantic validation for messages that look sensitive.

remediation.issue: Approved learnings modify CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.
remediation.suggestion: Create backups before edits and keep dry-run previews available for every write path.

remediation.issue: Legacy shell scripts remain in the package.
remediation.suggestion: Remove unused legacy scripts or clearly mark them as examples so installers do not execute stale implementations.

content.value_statement: Useful corrections are easy to lose between coding sessions. Claude Reflect captures them, reviews them with you, and applies approved learnings to memory files.
actual_capabilities: Detects correction and preference phrases from Claude Code prompt hooks.
Stores queued learnings in the local Claude Code learnings queue.
Provides /reflect, /skip-reflect, and /view-queue commands for review workflows.
Scans Claude Code session history when /reflect --scan-history is used.
Applies approved learnings to CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files.
Can analyze repeated tool errors and propose project-specific guidance.
limitations: Requires local access to Claude Code memory and session files.
Pattern detection can capture false positives, so review is required.
Semantic validation depends on the Claude CLI being available locally.
It does not verify that saved learnings remain correct over time.

use_cases.title: Maintain Team Conventions
use_cases.description: Capture repeated coding corrections and save approved conventions for future Claude Code sessions.

use_cases.title: Remember Personal Preferences
use_cases.description: Turn personal tool, model, and workflow preferences into reviewed memory entries.

use_cases.title: Review Repeated Tool Errors
use_cases.description: Find recurring project errors and convert approved fixes into project-specific guidance.

prompt_templates.title: View Pending Learnings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /view-queue to show my current queued learnings before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review And Apply
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /reflect and ask before changing global or project memory files.

prompt_templates.title: Scan Recent History
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /reflect --scan-history --days 14 and review only project-specific corrections.

prompt_templates.title: Deduplicate Memory Entries
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /reflect --dedupe, compare similar CLAUDE.md entries, and ask me before consolidating them.

output_examples.input: A user says to remember a preferred package manager.
output_examples.output: A queued learning appears for review with its suggested scope and confidence.

output_examples.input: A developer runs a history scan after several coding sessions.
output_examples.output: The command lists candidate learnings and asks which entries should be saved.

output_examples.input: A project has repeated database connection errors.
output_examples.output: The workflow proposes a project memory entry about checking local environment configuration.

best_practices: Review every proposed learning before applying it to memory files.
Use project scope for repository-specific tools, paths, and conventions.
Run dry-run or queue review before large history scans.
anti_patterns: Do not save secrets, tokens, database URLs, or private customer data as learnings.
Do not run broad history scans on shared machines without user consent.
Do not apply low-confidence or stale learnings without editing them first.

faq.question: Does Claude Reflect change files automatically?
faq.answer: The workflow is designed to ask for review before applying learnings to memory files.

faq.question: Where does it store queued learnings?
faq.answer: It stores candidate learnings in the local Claude Code learnings queue under the user home directory.

faq.question: Can it scan old Claude Code sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. The /reflect --scan-history command can inspect local session history for missed corrections.

faq.question: Does it support AGENTS.md?
faq.answer: Yes. It can sync approved learnings to AGENTS.md when that file exists in the project.

faq.question: Can false positives happen?
faq.answer: Yes. Correction patterns are heuristic, so users should review, edit, or skip each candidate.

faq.question: Is this skill suitable for sensitive projects?
faq.answer: Use caution. It reads session history and memory files, so redact sensitive data before saving learnings.
